q: Distance travelled by the body is the _____ of the path along which the body moves.
e: Distance travelled by the body is the length of the path along which the body moves. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start. Displacement: the straight directed change from start point to end point.

q: Displacement is the distance travelled along a _____.
e: Displacement is the distance travelled along a particular direction. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start. Curved path: a bent path, which light does not take in a uniform medium.

q: Distance has no specific direction. It has only magnitude; and therefore, it is a _____.
e: Distance has no specific direction. It has only magnitude; and therefore, it is a scalar. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. Vector: a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

q: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; and therefore, it is a _____.
e: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; and therefore, it is a vector. Vector here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. Scalar: a quantity that has magnitude only.

q: The average speed, $v_{av}$, is the ratio of total distance $s$ to _____.
e: The average speed, $v_{av}$, is the ratio of total distance $s$ to time taken $t$. Time taken $t$ here means the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force. Displacement: the straight directed change from start point to end point.

q: The average velocity, $\vec{v}_{av}$, is the ratio of total displacement $\vec{s}$ to _____.
e: The average velocity, $\vec{v}_{av}$, is the ratio of total displacement $\vec{s}$ to time taken $t$. Time taken $t$ here means the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force. Total distance $s$: the path length travelled, with no direction.

q: If the starting point and the end point are the same, the total displacement is zero. Therefore, average velocity is _____.
e: If the starting point and the end point are the same, the total displacement is zero. Therefore, average velocity is zero. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The speed (or) velocity at a particular instant of time are referred to as _____ speed and _____ velocity.
e: The speed (or) velocity at a particular instant of time are referred to as instantaneous speed and instantaneous velocity. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Instantaneous speed is defined as the limiting value of $\frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$ as time $\Delta t$ approaches _____.
e: Instantaneous speed is defined as the limiting value of $\frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$ as time $\Delta t$ approaches zero. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the time rate of change of _____.
e: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the time rate of change of displacement. Displacement here means the straight directed change from start point to end point. Distance: the path length travelled, with no direction.

q: Motion with constant velocity is known as _____ motion.
e: Motion with constant velocity is known as uniform motion. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity involving velocity.

q: If either magnitude (or) direction (or) both magnitude and direction of the velocity changes, the body is said to have an _____.
e: If either magnitude (or) direction (or) both magnitude and direction of the velocity changes, the body is said to have an acceleration. Acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes.

q: The average acceleration $a_{av}$ is defined by the equation $a_{av} =$ _____.
e: The average acceleration $a_{av}$ is defined by the equation $a_{av} =$ $\frac{v - v_0}{t}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of _____.
e: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity. Velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Distance: the path length travelled, with no direction.

q: Acceleration is said to be positive if the magnitude of velocity is _____.
e: Acceleration is said to be positive if the magnitude of velocity is increasing. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Negative acceleration is usually called _____ or retardation.
e: Negative acceleration is usually called deceleration or retardation. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing. Acceleration: how quickly velocity changes.
